versions.provenance: 8th edition breast TNM, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
The 8th edition staging system applies to invasive and in situ carcinomas of both the female and male breast. T is based on invasive tumour size, N on the location and number of involved regional nodes, and M on distant spread; the node-count definitions (1 to 3, 4 to 9, 10 or more) apply to pathologic N, while clinical N is defined by node location and fixation.

The major change in 8th edition is the addition of prognostic stage groups that combine the anatomic T, N and M with histologic grade and biomarker status (ER, PR and HER2), plus multigene panel results in selected node-negative, ER-positive, HER2-negative tumours; the prognostic stage frequently differs from the anatomic stage, so both should be reported when biomarkers are available. Lobular carcinoma in situ is no longer classified as Tis. The stage groups listed below are the anatomic groups (T, N and M only); the prognostic stage groups add grade and biomarkers on top of them.

t.label: Carcinoma in situ: ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS); or Paget disease of the nipple not associated with invasive carcinoma or DCIS in the underlying breast parenchyma
Tumour > 1 mm but <= 5 mm in greatest dimension
Tumour > 5 mm but <= 10 mm in greatest dimension
Tumour > 10 mm but <= 20 mm in greatest dimension
Tumour > 20 mm but <= 50 mm in greatest dimension
Tumour of any size with direct extension to the chest wall and/or to the skin (ulceration or macroscopic skin nodules); invasion of the dermis alone does not qualify
Extension to the chest wall; invasion of or adherence to pectoralis muscle alone, without chest wall structures, does not qualify
Ulceration and/or ipsilateral macroscopic satellite skin nodules and/or oedema (including peau d'orange) that does not meet the criteria for inflammatory carcinoma

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed (for example, previously removed)
Metastasis to movable ipsilateral level I and/or level II axillary lymph node(s)
Micrometastases (approximately 200 cells, larger than 0.2 mm but none larger than 2.0 mm)
Metastasis in ipsilateral level I/II axillary nodes that are clinically fixed or matted; or in clinically detected ipsilateral internal mammary nodes in the absence of axillary node metastasis
Metastasis in ipsilateral level I/II axillary nodes fixed to one another (matted) or to other structures
Metastasis only in clinically detected ipsilateral internal mammary node(s) and without axillary node metastasis
Metastasis in ipsilateral infraclavicular (level III axillary) node(s); or in internal mammary node(s) with level I/II axillary node involvement; or in ipsilateral supraclavicular node(s)
Metastasis in ipsilateral infraclavicular (level III axillary) node(s) with or without level I/II axillary node involvement
Metastasis in ipsilateral internal mammary node(s) and level I/II axillary node(s)

m.label: No clinical or radiographic evidence of distant metastasis

No clinical or radiographic evidence of distant metastasis, but molecularly or microscopically detected tumour cell deposits <= 0.2 mm in circulating blood, bone marrow, or non-regional nodes, in a patient without symptoms or signs of metastasis
Distant metastasis detected by clinical and radiographic means, and/or histologically proven metastasis larger than 0.2 mm

postNeoadjuvant.note: After neoadjuvant systemic therapy, staging uses ypT and ypN with the same anatomic stage groups as the pathologic table; a complete pathologic response (ypT0/is ypN0) is recorded but is not assigned a stage group. Prognostic-stage assignment still incorporates grade and biomarkers.

versions.regionalNodes: Ipsilateral axillary nodes (level I low axilla, level II mid axilla, and level III infraclavicular/apical), ipsilateral internal mammary (parasternal) nodes, and ipsilateral supraclavicular nodes. Any other nodal metastasis (including contralateral or cervical nodes) is classified as distant metastasis (M1).
versions.histologicGrade: Nottingham combined histologic grade (Elston-Ellis modification of Scarff-Bloom-Richardson), scoring tubule formation, nuclear pleomorphism, and mitotic count (each 1 to 3): total 3 to 5 = G1 (low grade), 6 to 7 = G2 (intermediate), 8 to 9 = G3 (high grade).
versions.histopathologicTypes: Invasive carcinoma of no special type (formerly invasive ductal carcinoma) is most common, followed by invasive lobular carcinoma. Special subtypes include tubular, mucinous (colloid), medullary, papillary, cribriform, and metaplastic carcinoma. In situ disease comprises DCIS and lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS is no longer classified as Tis in the 8th Edition).
prognosticFactors: Multigene recurrence scores (for example Oncotype DX) in selected ER-positive HER2-negative tumours
